title: How JavaScript Reaches the CPU

content.explanation: Computers cannot directly understand JavaScript code. CPUs only execute machine instructions. JavaScript engines such as V8 act as translators between JavaScript and the processor. When JavaScript code is executed, V8 parses it, compiles it into machine instructions, and sends those instructions to the CPU. This process allows developers to write human-readable code while computers execute low-level operations efficiently.
content.example: When console.log('Hello') runs in Chrome, V8 converts the instruction into machine code before execution.
content.analogy: A translator converts a book from one language into another language understood by the reader.
content.keyTakeaway: JavaScript must be translated before the CPU can execute it.

revisionSummary: V8 converts JavaScript into machine instructions.

mcqs.question: What does a JavaScript engine do?
mcqs.explanation: JavaScript engines execute JavaScript by translating it into machine instructions.

mcqs.question: Why can't CPUs run JavaScript directly?
mcqs.explanation: CPUs execute machine instructions, not JavaScript syntax.
